subject: Chemistry
unit: Unit I — Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
title: Empirical Formulas, Molecular Formulas & Combustion Analysis
quickSummary: Empirical formula gives the simplest atomic ratio, while molecular formula gives actual atom counts. In combustion analysis, anhydrous CaCl₂ absorbs water and concentrated KOH absorbs carbon dioxide to calculate elemental percentages.
summary: Master the quantitative cascade from combustion tube data to exact molecular formula determination.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4. Formula Determination Cascade
conceptBreakdown.title: 4. Formula Determination Cascade

summaryBox.title: Formula Cascade Rule
summaryBox.takeaway: Mass % → Relative Mole Ratio → Simple Integer Ratio → Empirical Formula → n = Molar Mass / EFM → Molecular Formula = (EF)_n.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FORMULA DETERMINATION CASCADE
                      
   Elemental Mass % ──► Relative Mole Ratio ──► Simple Whole-Number Ratio ──► Empirical Formula
                                                                                  │
   Molecular Formula ($MF = (EF)_n$) ◄── $n = \frac{\text{Molar Mass}}{\text{Empirical Mass}}$ ┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Empirical Formula (EF)**: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
• **Molecular Formula (MF)**: The actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule: $\mathbf{MF = [EF]_n}$.
• **Integer Multiplier**: $\mathbf{n = \frac{\text{Molar Mass (M)}}{\text{Empirical Formula Mass (EFM)}}}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Quantitative Combustion Analysis Chemistry
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Quantitative Combustion Analysis Chemistry
conceptBreakdown.content:
For a pure organic compound $\text{C}_x\text{H}_y\text{O}_z$ undergoing complete combustion in excess $\text{O}_2$:

$$\text{C}_x\text{H}_y\text{O}_z + \left(x + \frac{y}{4} - \frac{z}{2}\right)\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow x \text{ CO}_2 (g) + \frac{y}{2} \text{ H}_2\text{O} (l)$$

**The Combustion Absorption Train**:
1. **Absorber 1 (Water)**: Anhydrous $\text{CaCl}_2$ or $\text{Mg(ClO}_4)_2$ absorbs $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
   $$\% \text{ Hydrogen} = \frac{2}{18} \times \frac{\text{Mass of }\text{H}_2\text{O}\text{ collected}}{\text{Mass of Organic Sample}} \times 100$$

2. **Absorber 2 (Carbon Dioxide)**: Concentrated $\text{KOH}$ solution (Ascharite) absorbs $\text{CO}_2$.
   $$\% \text{ Carbon} = \frac{12}{44} \times \frac{\text{Mass of }\text{CO}_2\text{ collected}}{\text{Mass of Organic Sample}} \times 100$$

3. **Oxygen Percentage**:
   $$\% \text{ Oxygen} = 100 - (\% \text{ C} + \% \text{ H} + \% \text{ Other Elements})$$

quickRevision: CaCl2 absorbs H2O; KOH absorbs CO2 in combustion analysis.
Oxygen % is always calculated by subtraction from 100%.
